ZEROTACKY
ZER
TACKY
HOME
HOW IT WORKS
FIND A SHOW
GYM DIRECTORY
ATHLETES
ACCOUNT
JOIN A MEET
How ZeroTacky Works

One site for the whole meet: the promoter builds it on a phone or laptop, athletes find and enter it here, volunteers join with a six-character code on the day, and everyone watches the same live scoreboard. Pick the track that fits you.

PROMOTERS
ATHLETES & SPECTATORS
VOLUNTEERS & JUDGES
FAQ
WHAT'S COMING
RUNNING A SHOW
Promoters

You set the meet up once, on your phone or a laptop. When you publish it, every judge, pit crew phone, and the public scoreboard see the same divisions, events, and scores, so nobody is working from a different copy.

1
Create an account and tick Promoter

Your account is what proves a meet is yours. Only you can change or delete it, and if you lose your phone you sign in on another one and everything is still there. There is nothing to write down or pass around between promoters.

Account
2
Build the meet

On My Meets, New Meet asks for a name and a date and opens the meet as eight tabs: details and rules (admin PIN, run order, tiebreaker, gym plates), divisions, stations, events, athletes, listing, registrations and meet day. The phone scorer can build the meet itself under Meet Setup, but listing it and approving registrations happen on My Meets. The first-show guide walks through every tab with pictures.

Set up your first show
3
List it and open entries

A new meet starts unlisted: it is not in Find a Show and has no show page yet, though its registration page and scoreboard open for anyone with the direct link. On the Listing tab you tick Listed to put it in Find a Show, fill in the venue and entry fee, and decide whether athletes can register right now, join a waitlist, or only enter on the day. Building on the phone instead? Publish from the scorer while signed in and the meet lands under My Meets the same way.

My Meets
4
Approve registrations

When an athlete registers, their entry appears on your Registrations tab with the division they picked and their signed waiver. Accepting them adds them to the roster for that division. You can also decline, or leave them pending while you sort out numbers.

5
Hand out the join code on meet day

The Meet Day tab shows a six-character code. Anyone helping you enters it on Join a Meet and their phone is connected to your meet. Judges and anyone who needs to change the setup also type in the admin PIN from step 1. If the code gets out to people who should not have it, tap rotate and the old one stops working.

Join a Meet
6
Share the live scoreboard

Every published meet gets a web page with the standings, each event's results and who is up next. The link is on the Meet Day tab. Put it on a TV in the gym with the TV layout and send it to spectators, who can open it on any phone without signing in.

See a demo board
Setting up your first show, step by step

One meet from a blank screen to posted results, with a picture of every screen and what each change does on the public side.

COMPETING AND WATCHING
Athletes & Spectators

Find a show, keep an eye on it, register when entries open, then follow the scoring live on the day. Shows marked DEMO are made up so you can see what a listing and a scoreboard look like; they do not take entries.

1
Find a show

Search by name, division, status, state, implement, or federation. Each show page has the venue, the divisions and events, and whether registration is open.

Find a Show
2
Follow it

If you are signed in you can tap Follow on a show you are thinking about. It then appears under Following on your My Meets page so you can find it again without searching. Following does not enter you in anything and the promoter is not told.

Account
3
Register

Once entries are open, sign in or create a free account on the form itself, then pick your division, give an emergency contact and your date of birth, and sign the waiver. You need to be 12 or older on the day of the meet. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian creates the account and fills in their part of the form.

4
Track it on My Meets

Your entry starts as Pending approval until the promoter looks at it, then becomes Registered, Waitlisted, or Declined. After the meet it moves to Completed, so over time My Meets becomes a record of where you have competed.

My Meets
5
Watch live

The scoreboard page updates as judges enter scores. If you are at the venue you can also enter the join code on Join a Meet and see the Next Up list, including the weights and heights for each athlete, without being able to change anything.

Join a Meet
MEET-DAY CREW
Volunteers & Judges

You do not need an account. The promoter gives you a six-character code, you pick what you are doing that day, and the app opens already set up for your job.

1
Enter the join code

Open Join a Meet and type the code. The meet name comes back so you can check it is the right one.

Join a Meet
2
Pick your role

Athlete or Spectator shows the standings and who is up next, with nothing to tap by accident. Volunteer is for pit crew and shows the plate loading calculator. Judge and Promoter need the admin PIN from the promoter; you type it once and the phone remembers which role you chose.

3
Judges: score from the pad

Pick the event and the athletes come up in the right order. Enter reps, time, distance, the bar height reached or stone splits, depending on the event. Scores go to the scoreboard the moment the phone has signal.

4
Pit crew: load from Next Up

Next Up shows who is lifting, the weight they need, the plates to put on each side and any rack or pin height, so nobody is doing plate maths at the bar. The promoter decides whether you can change the bar weight or enter a custom load.

5
Lose signal? Keep going

The app keeps working with no signal. Anything you enter is held on the phone and sent as soon as it reconnects, so a dead spot in the gym does not cost you any scores.

COMMON QUESTIONS
FAQ
EVERYONE
Does it cost anything?
No. Finding shows, registering, running a meet, the live scoreboard and the gym directory are all free right now. If that changes for any part of it, the price will be on the page before you use it, and what is already free for athletes stays free.
Does it work without Wi-Fi?
Yes. Scoring happens on the phone and is held there until it can be sent. A judge can score a whole event with no signal, and the public scoreboard catches up when the phone reconnects.
Do I need to install an app?
No. Everything runs in the browser on any phone, tablet or laptop. Promoters and judges can add the scorer to the home screen so it opens like an app, but nothing is downloaded from a store. Open the scorer
I forgot my password.
On the sign-in form, enter your email and tap Forgot password. The email you get has a link that brings you back to the Account page to choose a new one. If you are already signed in, use Change password on the same page. Account
What happens to my data?
What you enter when you register goes to the promoter of that meet, and ZeroTacky keeps what it needs to run the service. Your email is never shown publicly. The Privacy Policy lists what is kept and for how long. Privacy Policy
ATHLETES AND SPECTATORS
Do I need an account to register for a show?
Yes, a free one, and you can create it right on the registration form without leaving the page. The entry is tied to your account: it shows on My Meets so you can see when the promoter accepts it, and after the meet it stays there as part of your record. You need to be 12 or older on the day of the meet; under 18, a parent or guardian creates the account, registers you and completes their part of the waiver. Find a Show
How do I watch a show live?
Open the show page and tap the live scoreboard link. It shows standings, each event and who is up next, and updates as judges score. No account, no code. If you are at the venue, the promoter can also give you the join code, which adds the Next Up list with each athlete's weights.
What shows up publicly about me?
Once the promoter accepts you, your name and division appear on the meet roster and the live scoreboard, the same as a printed start list. Your email, date of birth and emergency contact go to the promoter only. Nothing else is public unless you turn on your own athlete page.
How do I get my own athlete page?
On your Account page, pick a username and turn on Show my profile publicly. Your name, photo, roles, location, home gym, favorite lift, PRs and the social handles you added show at zerotacky.com/athletes/yourname and in the Athletes list. Turn it off any time and the page is gone. Athletes
PROMOTERS
What do I need to run a show on ZeroTacky?
An account with Promoter ticked, your phone or a laptop to set the meet up, and one phone per judge on the day. Nothing is installed and the gym does not need Wi-Fi. The first-show guide walks through the whole thing with pictures. Set up your first show
Join code or admin PIN: who gets which?
Two codes, two jobs. The six-character join code gets a phone into your meet; give it to everyone helping, and to athletes or spectators who want the Next Up list. The admin PIN lets a joined phone score and change the setup; give it to judges and your co-promoters only. The join code is on the Meet Day tab; the PIN is set on the Meet tab.
Can other people help me run it?
Yes. Anyone with the join code and the admin PIN can judge or edit from their phone; several phones can score different stations at the same time and everything merges. The meet itself belongs to your account, so only you can list, unlist or delete it.
How do athletes get on the roster?
Two ways, and you can mix them. Open registration on the Listing tab and athletes register from the show page; each entry appears on your Registrations tab and you accept or decline it (Waitlist Only on the Listing tab holds new entries instead). Or type athletes straight into the roster in Meet Setup, which is what most people do for a small show or for day-of entries.
Can I unlist or delete a meet?
Unlist any time from the Listing tab; the meet stays yours, it just leaves Find a Show. Delete from the Meet Day tab as long as the meet is not running or finished; if it already has athletes or results you type its name to confirm. Finished meets are kept so results stay available. My Meets
GYM OWNERS
My gym is in the directory. How do I claim it?
Open the gym's page and tap Claim this gym, then give your name, email and role at the gym. Sign in first and the approved listing attaches to your account straight away; otherwise we confirm by email. We check each claim against the gym's own site or contact address. Once approved, the listing is yours to edit from My Gym: equipment, day passes, drop-in hours, website and contact. Gym Directory
My gym is not listed. How do I add it?
Sign in, tick Gym owner on your Account page, and use Add my gym. It goes into a short review queue so the directory stays real gyms with real equipment, then appears under your account. Add my gym
NOT HERE YET
What's coming

Everything above is live today and free. These are the next pieces, in roughly the order we plan to build them.

Paid show registration

Promoters set an entry fee and athletes pay when they register, instead of settling up separately.

Day passes from the gym directory

Buy a drop-in pass for a listed gym from its page, so travelling athletes can train on the way to a show.

Trainer directory

Coaches who train in person or online get their own searchable list, built from the trainer flag on athlete profiles.

Show history on athlete pages

Meets you competed in, with placings, listed on your public page once the promoter marks the show complete.

Gyms and shows linked both ways

A show page points at its host gym, and a gym page lists the shows it has hosted.

ZEROTACKY
ZER
TACKY

Your one stop for strongman: shows, registration, live scoring, and a gym directory.

ZEROTACKY
ZER
TACKY
HOME
HOW IT WORKS
FIND A SHOW
GYM DIRECTORY
ATHLETES
ACCOUNT
JOIN A MEET
How It Works
 PROMOTER GUIDE
Set up your first show

This walks one made-up meet, the Iron Harbor Classic, from a blank screen to meet day. Every screen below is the real one you will use, and each step says what it changes for athletes and spectators. Budget about half an hour the first time.

WHAT YOU NEED
A ZeroTacky account with Promoter ticked on the Account page. The meet belongs to that account, so it follows you from laptop to phone and only you can change it.
A laptop for the setup. The phone scorer can build the meet itself under Meet Setup (divisions, stations, events, athletes), but Listing and Registrations live on My Meets only, and the tabs are easier to read on a bigger screen.
On the day: one phone per judge and one for the pit crew. Volunteers do not need accounts; they join with a code you hand out in step 9.
1
Create the meet
2
Meet details and rules
3
Divisions
4
Stations and floor plan
5
Events
6
Athletes
7
List it and open entries
8
Approve registrations
9
Meet day codes and screens
10
The live scoreboard
1
MY MEETS, NEW MEET
Create the meet

Open My Meets and tap New Meet. It asks for the name, the competition date and an optional web address. The address (the slug) becomes zerotacky.com/shows/your-slug; leave it blank and one is made from the name.

Create & Open Meet saves the meet to your account and opens it as eight numbered tabs. The order of the tabs is the order you fill them in.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Nothing yet. A new meet starts unlisted, so it is not in Find a Show and has no show page until you tick Listed in step 6. Its registration page and live scoreboard do open by direct link, which is handy for checking your work before anyone else sees it.

My Meets
2
TAB 1, MEET
Meet details and rules

The admin PIN is four to six digits. Judges and anyone who needs to change the setup on meet day type it once on their phone, after the join code from step 9. Collar weight is per pair and is added to every bar load the pit crew calculator shows.

Athlete run order decides who lifts when. Reverse Overall Points is the usual choice: the leader goes last so the podium race builds. Reverse Previous Event looks only at the last event. Roster Order never reshuffles. The screen explains each one under the buttons.

The tiebreaker only matters when two athletes finish on the same points. Available Gym Plates tells the pit crew calculator what it is allowed to use; turn off anything the gym does not own.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

The run order drives the Next Up queue on volunteer phones; the public scoreboard only shows who is Up Now on each station. Plates and collars drive the loads the pit crew sees. None of this is shown to athletes directly.

3
TAB 2, DIVISIONS
Divisions

Add one division per weight class or experience group, named the way athletes expect to read them. Type a name and press Add; the arrows reorder them.

The order here is the order they appear everywhere else: the registration dropdown, the scoreboard and the show card. Edits sit in working memory until you press Save Changes in the banner at the bottom.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Division names show as chips on the show card in Find a Show, as the choices on the registration form and as the sections of the live scoreboard.

4
TAB 3, STATIONS
Stations and floor plan

A station is one set of implements running its own order. Divisions on the same station run back to back; two stations run at the same time in different parts of the gym.

A small meet is fine on one station. Most promoters decide this after sign-ups close, when they know how many athletes each division has. Rename the stations if the gym calls them something else. If one station runs the events in a different order from the rest, the arrows on its card set that order.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Each station gets an Up Now strip at the top of the scoreboard, so spectators can see who is lifting where. Next Up on the volunteer phones is per station.

5
TAB 4, EVENTS
Events

Add Event opens the form. Pick how it is scored (reps, max weight, time or distance, time or implements), set the time cap and lanes, then tell the loader how the implement works: load points is how many places plates go on, tare is what the empty implement weighs. Those two numbers are what make the pit crew plate maths right.

Under per-division weights, enter the target weight for each division. Add a callout title if the pit crew should see a note, for example the keg or the pin height. Save Event, then Save Changes.

Events run in the order listed. Use the arrows on the cards if the running order changes.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Implement names show as chips on the show card. The registration page lists every division with its target weight for each event, so athletes know what they are signing up to lift. In the TV layout the scoreboard gets one column per event.

6
TAB 5, ATHLETES
Athletes

There are two ways onto the roster. Athletes who register online land here when you accept them in step 8. Paper sign-ups and walk-ins you add yourself: Bulk Add takes one name per line into a division, Single Add takes one at a time.

Each athlete gets a lot number inside their division. That is the order for the first event, and the fallback order whenever two athletes are level. The one exception is Reverse Previous Event, which breaks a tie on the last event by overall points first and lot number second.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Roster names appear on the live scoreboard as soon as the meet is listed, with a dash in every event column until scores come in. Add only athletes you expect to show up.

7
TAB 6, LISTING
List it and open entries

Tick Listed to put the meet in Find a Show. The three status dropdowns are the badges the public sees: competition status (upcoming, live, completed), registration status (open, waitlist, closed, day-of only) and results status.

Fill in the venue, the federation or format, the entry fee as you want it displayed, the deadline, an athlete cap and a contact. No money moves through the site; the fee line tells athletes how you want to be paid. Save Listing Settings writes it straight to the server.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

This tab is the public face of the show. The card in Find a Show, the show page and the top of the registration page are all built from it, and the capacity line counts every athlete on the roster against your cap, including the ones you added by hand.

Find a Show
The card athletes see in Find a Show.
The show page at zerotacky.com/shows/your-slug.
8
TAB 7, REGISTRATIONS
Approve registrations

An athlete signs in or creates a free account on the form, picks a division, gives a name, email, emergency contact and date of birth, signs the waiver and submits. The entry is tied to their account, which is how it shows on their My Meets page. Under-18s are entered by a parent or guardian from the guardian's account.

Each entry shows up here as Pending with the division and the signed waiver. Accept adds the athlete to that division roster with the next lot number; Decline removes them. Emergency contacts and dates of birth are visible to you only.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

The athlete sees Pending, then Registered or Declined, on their My Meets page. An entry only takes a spot on the capacity line once you accept it and it joins the roster; pending entries do not count.

What the athlete sees first: the account step.
Then the entry form, with name and email filled from the account.
What you see.
9
TAB 8, MEET DAY
Meet day codes and screens

The six-character join code is how volunteer phones attach to your meet. Print Both gives you two QR codes for the gym wall: one for judges and pit crew, one for the live scoreboard. Rotate the code if it gets out to people who should not have it; phones signed in to your account are unaffected.

Volunteers open Join a Meet, enter the code and pick a role. Athlete and Spectator are read-only. Pit crew get the loading calculator. Judge and Promoter also type the admin PIN from step 2.

Your own phone joins the same way: open the join link, pick Promoter and enter the admin PIN. Opening the scorer on its own shows whatever meet that phone had last, so always come in through the join link. The TV link is a full-width standings table for a laptop plugged into the gym TV.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

The scoreboard link is public and needs no sign-in. Share it with spectators and put the TV layout on a screen in the gym.

Join a Meet
What a volunteer sees after scanning the join QR.
10
ZEROTACKY.COM/M/YOUR-SLUG
The live scoreboard

As judges score, the board updates on every phone and TV that has it open. On a phone each division shows standing cards plus the current event. The TV layout, from the Phone/TV button in the header or the TV link on Meet Day, gives each division its own table with one column per event and the total on the right. In both, the strips at the top show who is up on each station and the chips filter to one division.

When the last event is in, go back to the Listing tab and set competition status to Completed and results to Final. The show moves to Completed on every athlete's My Meets page and the standings stay up as the record of the day.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

This is the page spectators share. It works on any phone with no app and no account, and it keeps the final standings after the show.

See a demo board
The TV layout. On a phone the same board shows standing cards.
After the show

Set the statuses to Completed and Final on the Listing tab and the show becomes a record: the public page and scoreboard stay up, and it moves to Completed on every athlete's My Meets. A video walkthrough of this guide is coming after our first full show.

ZeroTacky Terms of Use
DRAFT FOR LEGAL REVIEW. Working draft for ZeroTacky; a qualified attorney should review it before it is relied on.

Effective date: October 2026
Operator: ZeroTacky, operated from the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, United States ("ZeroTacky", "we")

1. Agreement

By creating an account, registering for a competition, publishing or scoring a meet, or otherwise using zerotacky.com and the ZeroTacky meet-day scoring app (together, the "Service"), you agree to these Terms and to our Privacy Policy. If you do not agree, do not use the Service.

2. What ZeroTacky is, and is not

ZeroTacky is software: a directory of strongman competitions, an athlete registration tool, and a scoring app that promoters and their volunteers run on their own phones on meet day.

ZeroTacky is not the organizer of any competition. Unless a competition page says otherwise, we do not organize, sanction, insure, supervise or officiate the competitions listed on the Service. The promoter does.
No safety or medical advice. Plate-loading math, implement weights and rack-height callouts in the Service are conveniences. Promoters, judges, loaders and athletes are responsible for checking bar weights, collars, pins and the course before every attempt.
Results are the promoter's. Scores and standings shown by the Service are entered by the promoter's judges. The promoter decides the official results and may correct them.
3. Accounts and age
You must be at least 13 years old to create an account. If you are under 18, a parent or legal guardian must agree to these Terms for you, and must complete any competition registration on your behalf (see section 4).
You are responsible for your login, and for any publish key, join code or admin PIN a promoter gives you. Do not share them beyond the people running the meet.
One person, one account. Keep your email address current; we use it for sign-in and for messages about your registrations.
You may close your account at any time from the account page or by emailing us (section 10). Competition records you appear in may remain in the promoter's results (section 7).
4. Registering for a competition
Registering on ZeroTacky sends a request to the promoter. The promoter accepts, declines or waitlists it. A request is not a confirmed entry until the promoter accepts it.
You must accept the competition waiver to register. The waiver is between you, the promoter, the venue and ZeroTacky, and is shown in full before you submit.
Athletes under 18 may not register themselves. A parent or legal guardian must complete the registration, accept the waiver on the athlete's behalf, and may be required by the promoter to attend check-in and sign on paper. Promoters set the minimum age for their competitions.
Entry fees, refunds, weigh-ins, membership cards and disputes are between you and the promoter. ZeroTacky does not currently collect payments.
Give accurate information. Promoters rely on your emergency contact on meet day.
5. Promoters

If you publish or score a meet on ZeroTacky you confirm that:

you are responsible for the safety, insurance, venue permission, rules, officiating, medical coverage and results of your event, and for deciding whether your event needs a waiver beyond the one shown by the Service;
you will use athlete registration data (names, emails, emergency contacts, bodyweights) only to run the competition the athlete registered for, and will delete or stop using it when it is no longer needed for that purpose;
you have the right to publish the event details, division names and results you upload;
you will keep your publish key, join codes and admin PIN to the people running your meet, and tell us if one leaks;
you will keep your own backup of your meet (the Service offers a JSON backup and CSV export) and will not rely on the Service as your only record.
6. Acceptable use

Do not: submit false or impersonated registrations; guess or brute-force another meet's codes, keys or PINs; interfere with live scoring; scrape athlete contact details; upload content you do not have the right to publish; or use the Service for anything unlawful. We may suspend or close accounts and remove meets that break these Terms or disrupt a live competition.

7. Public results and your name

Promoters may publicly list their meets. For a listed or published meet, division rosters, athlete names, bodyweight classes, scores and placings are public on the Service and may stay in the competition archive. Email addresses and emergency contacts are never public. If you want your name removed from a past result, contact the promoter first; if that fails, contact us (section 10) and we will work it out with the promoter.

8. Free of charge, "as is"

The Service is currently free. THE SERVICE IS PROVIDED "AS IS" AND "AS AVAILABLE", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NON-INFRINGEMENT. WE DO NOT PROMISE THAT THE SERVICE WILL BE UNINTERRUPTED, ERROR-FREE OR FREE OF DATA LOSS. Scores entered on a phone that is offline are queued on that phone and may be lost if the phone is lost, reset or offline for a long time.

9. Limitation of liability

TO THE FULLEST EXTENT THE LAW ALLOWS, ZEROTACKY AND ITS OPERATOR ARE NOT LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, OR FOR LOST PROFITS, DATA OR GOODWILL, OR FOR PERSONAL INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE, ARISING FROM (1) YOUR PARTICIPATION IN ANY COMPETITION OR TRAINING, (2) ANY SCORING ERROR, LOADING CALCULATION, RACK-HEIGHT CALLOUT OR SYNC DELAY, OR (3) YOUR USE OF OR INABILITY TO USE THE SERVICE. OUR TOTAL LIABILITY FOR ALL CLAIMS IS LIMITED TO THE GREATER OF ONE HUNDRED U.S. DOLLARS ($100) OR THE AMOUNT YOU PAID ZEROTACKY IN THE TWELVE MONTHS BEFORE THE CLAIM. Some states do not allow some of these limits; in those states they apply as far as the law allows.

10. Contact and changes

Questions, deletion requests and complaints: privacy@zerotacky.com. If we change these Terms in a way that matters, we will update the effective date and tell account holders by email before the change takes effect. Continuing to use the Service after that is acceptance of the new Terms.

11. Governing law and venue

These Terms are governed by the law of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, without regard to conflict-of-laws rules. Disputes about these Terms or the Service go to the state or federal courts in or serving York County, Pennsylvania, and you consent to their jurisdiction. Nothing in this section changes the governing law stated in a competition waiver.

1. What ZeroTacky is

2. What we collect and why

Anyone with an account (athletes, promoters)	Email address, display name, password (stored hashed by our authentication provider), sign-in timestamps	To sign you in, let promoters manage their meets, and send you messages about your registrations	You
Athletes who register for a competition	Name, email, emergency contact (name and phone), the division you chose, optional bodyweight, your date of birth, the date and time you accepted the waiver and an identifier of the exact waiver text you accepted; for an athlete under 18 on competition day, the parent or guardian's name and contact	To send your entry to the promoter, put you on the roster when accepted, and give the promoter your emergency contact on meet day	You, or your parent or guardian
Athletes on a meet roster (added by a promoter, with or without an account)	Name, division, lot number, optional bodyweight and rack heights, scores and placings	To run and score the meet and show standings	The promoter and their judges
Everyone who visits	Standard server logs (IP address, browser type, pages requested, timestamps) kept by our hosting provider; the IP address of a device that submits a registration or tries a PIN, kept for about a day to stop abuse	To keep the site running and stop brute-force and spam	Your browser

We do not run advertising trackers or sell data. We do not collect payment details; entry fees are between you and the promoter.

3. Cookies and storage on your device
Sign-in: a session token from our authentication provider (Supabase Auth) keeps you signed in.
Local storage: your theme and layout choice, and, if you use the scoring app (/scorer, /join), the meet you are working on, recovery snapshots and a queue of scores waiting to sync. Scores entered while the gym Wi-Fi is down stay on the phone and are sent when it reconnects. Clearing your browser data removes them.
No third-party advertising or cross-site tracking cookies.
4. Who sees your data
Promoters. When you register for a competition, the promoter of that competition gets your registration (name, email, emergency contact, date of birth, division, bodyweight if given, waiver acceptance, and guardian details for an athlete under 18). Promoters agree to use it only to run that competition.
The public. For a meet the promoter has listed or published, rosters, athlete names, divisions, scores and placings are public on /shows/<meet> and the live scoreboard /m/<meet>. Emails, emergency contacts and guardian details are never public.
Our providers. Vercel (hosting, United States), Supabase (database and authentication, United States) and Resend (transactional email, United States) process data for us under their own terms. We do not share data with anyone else except as the law requires.
5. How long we keep it
Account data: while your account exists. Close your account and we delete the profile within 30 days; your name may remain in competition results you took part in (below).
Registrations: until the promoter deletes the meet, or until you ask us to remove yours.
Results: published competition results are part of the sport's record and stay up unless the promoter removes the meet or you ask for your name to be removed from a past result.
Abuse-prevention IP records: about a day. Server logs: per our hosting provider's retention.
6. Your choices

Email privacy@zerotacky.com to see what we hold about you, correct it, delete your account or registrations, or have your name removed from a past result. We answer within 30 days. We may need to confirm you are the account holder first. Residents of states with privacy laws that give extra rights (for example California) can exercise them the same way.

7. Children

Nobody under 13 may create an account, and we do not knowingly collect information about anyone under 13. Athletes under 18 are registered for competitions by a parent or legal guardian, who provides the information in section 2. If you believe a child has given us information without a guardian's involvement, email us and we will delete it.

8. Security

Data is encrypted in transit; passwords are hashed by Supabase Auth; database access is restricted by row-level rules so promoters see only their own meets and athlete contact details are never readable by the public. No system is perfectly secure; if we learn of a breach affecting you we will tell you as the law requires.

9. Changes

If we change this policy in a way that matters (for example, when we add payments), we will update the effective date and email account holders before the change takes effect.

In this agreement, "I" and "me" mean the athlete, or, if the athlete is under 18, the athlete's parent or legal guardian signing on the athlete's behalf (see section 7). "Released Parties" means everyone listed in section 4.

1. The risks of strongman competition

I understand that competing in and warming up for strongman events, including overhead pressing (logs, axles, circus dumbbells, kegs), deadlifts, moving events (yokes, farmer's walks, Husafell stones, sandbags, vehicle and harness pulls) and loading events (Atlas stones, kegs, natural stones), involves heavy, awkward and moving implements and maximal physical effort.

I understand that these risks cannot be removed no matter how careful the Promoter, the Venue, the judges or the loaders are. They include, without limitation:

muscle tears, tendon and ligament ruptures (biceps, patellar, Achilles, rotator cuff), spinal injuries, hernias, fractures, concussions and crush injuries from dropped or shifting implements;
cardiovascular events, heat illness, blacking out under load, cuts and skin tears;
equipment failure, rack or yoke pins set at the wrong height, plates or collars slipping, uneven or wet floors and parking surfaces, and mistakes by volunteer loaders, spotters or judges;
permanent disability and death.
2. My fitness and my duty to inspect

I state that I am in good health, have trained for the weights and events of this competition, and have no medical condition that makes my participation unsafe. I am responsible for inspecting the course, the rack and yoke heights and the implements before each attempt, and for telling a judge or the Promoter at once if I believe anything is unsafe. I will follow the rules of the competition and the instructions of the judges and staff.

3. Medical treatment

If I am injured or have a medical emergency at the competition, I authorize the Promoter, Venue staff and medical personnel to give first aid and to arrange emergency transport and treatment. I am responsible for all medical, ambulance and hospital costs incurred for me.

4. Assumption of risk and release

In exchange for being allowed to register for and compete in {{EVENT_NAME}}, I voluntarily accept all risks of participating, known and unknown. On behalf of myself, my heirs, assigns and personal representatives, I release, waive, discharge and agree not to sue:

{{PROMOTER_NAME}} and its owners, officers, event staff, judges, loaders, spotters and volunteers;
the owner and operator of {{VENUE_NAME_AND_ADDRESS}} and their staff; and
ZeroTacky, the registration and scoring software provider, and its owner, operator and contributors,

from all liability, claims, demands and causes of action for any loss, damage, injury or death I suffer while participating in, warming up for, traveling to or from, or attending the competition, including loss caused by the ordinary negligence of any Released Party, to the fullest extent the law allows.

5. Indemnity

I agree to indemnify and hold harmless the Released Parties from any claim, loss, cost or expense (including reasonable attorney's fees) brought by me or on my behalf, or by any third party, arising from my participation in the competition or from my breach of this agreement, to the fullest extent the law allows.

6. Results, name and image

I agree that the Promoter and ZeroTacky may record and publish my name, division, bodyweight class, scores and placings, and photographs and video of me at the competition, on live scoreboards, in competition archives and in promotion of the competition and of ZeroTacky, without payment to me.

7. Athletes under 18

An athlete under 18 may not register on their own. If the athlete is under 18, I confirm that I am the athlete's parent or court-appointed legal guardian, that I am completing this registration for the athlete, that I have read this agreement, and that I agree to it both on the athlete's behalf and on my own behalf, including the release in section 4 and the indemnity in section 5 for any claim the athlete may later bring. I understand the Promoter may require my presence and a paper signature at check-in before the athlete competes, and that the Promoter sets the minimum age for this competition. I will give the Promoter my name and a way to reach me.

8. Scoring software

I understand that ZeroTacky is software run by the Promoter and its volunteers. Scores, standings, plate-loading calculations and rack-height callouts shown by the software are tools for the Promoter; the Promoter and the judges decide results and are responsible for checking weights and equipment. Scores may be delayed, corrected or lost if a device is offline. I release ZeroTacky from any claim about scoring errors, lost data or placings.

9. Electronic acceptance, copies and general terms

By checking the acceptance box and submitting my registration I sign this agreement electronically, and I agree that this has the same effect as a handwritten signature. ZeroTacky records the date and time of my acceptance and an identifier of the exact text I accepted. The current text is available at any time at zerotacky.com/legal/waiver; I can print or save it from that page or ask the Promoter for a copy.

I have read this agreement, I understand that I am giving up substantial legal rights by signing it, and I sign it freely. If any part of it is held invalid, the rest stays in force. This agreement is governed by the law of the state where the competition is held, unless the Promoter's own registration terms say otherwise.

ZEROTACKY
ZER
TACKY
HOME
HOW IT WORKS
FIND A SHOW

ACCOUNT
JOIN A MEET
How ZeroTacky Works

One site for the whole meet: the promoter builds it on a phone or laptop, athletes find and enter it here, volunteers join with a six-character code on the day, and everyone watches the same live scoreboard. Pick the track that fits you.

PROMOTERS
ATHLETES & SPECTATORS
VOLUNTEERS & JUDGES
FAQ
WHAT'S COMING
RUNNING A SHOW
Promoters

You set the meet up once, on your phone or a laptop. When you publish it, every judge, pit crew phone, and the public scoreboard see the same divisions, events, and scores, so nobody is working from a different copy.

1
Create an account and tick Promoter

Your account is what proves a meet is yours. Only you can change or delete it, and if you lose your phone you sign in on another one and everything is still there. There is nothing to write down or pass around between promoters.

Account
2
Build the meet

On My Meets, New Meet asks for a name and a date and opens the meet as eight tabs: details and rules (admin PIN, run order, tiebreaker, gym plates), divisions, stations, events, athletes, listing, registrations and meet day. The phone scorer can build the meet itself under Meet Setup, but listing it and approving registrations happen on My Meets. The first-show guide walks through every tab with pictures.

Set up your first show
3
List it and open entries

A new meet starts unlisted: it is not in Find a Show and has no show page yet, though its registration page and scoreboard open for anyone with the direct link. On the Listing tab you tick Listed to put it in Find a Show, fill in the venue and entry fee, and decide whether athletes can register right now, join a waitlist, or only enter on the day. Building on the phone instead? Publish from the scorer while signed in and the meet lands under My Meets the same way.

My Meets
4
Approve registrations

When an athlete registers, their entry appears on your Registrations tab with the division they picked and their signed waiver. Accepting them adds them to the roster for that division. You can also decline, or leave them pending while you sort out numbers.

5
Hand out the join code on meet day

The Meet Day tab shows a six-character code. Anyone helping you enters it on Join a Meet and their phone is connected to your meet. Judges and anyone who needs to change the setup also type in the admin PIN from step 1. If the code gets out to people who should not have it, tap rotate and the old one stops working.

Join a Meet
6
Share the live scoreboard

Every published meet gets a web page with the standings, each event's results and who is up next. The link is on the Meet Day tab. Put it on a TV in the gym with the TV layout and send it to spectators, who can open it on any phone without signing in.

See a demo board
Setting up your first show, step by step

One meet from a blank screen to posted results, with a picture of every screen and what each change does on the public side.

COMPETING AND WATCHING
Athletes & Spectators

Find a show, keep an eye on it, register when entries open, then follow the scoring live on the day. Shows marked DEMO are made up so you can see what a listing and a scoreboard look like; they do not take entries.

1
Find a show

Search by name, division, status, state, implement, or federation. Each show page has the venue, the divisions and events, and whether registration is open.

Find a Show
2
Follow it

If you are signed in you can tap Follow on a show you are thinking about. It then appears under Following on your My Meets page so you can find it again without searching. Following does not enter you in anything and the promoter is not told.

Account
3
Register

Once entries are open, sign in or create a free account on the form itself, then pick your division, give an emergency contact and your date of birth, and sign the waiver. You need to be 12 or older on the day of the meet. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian creates the account and fills in their part of the form.

4
Track it on My Meets

Your entry starts as Pending approval until the promoter looks at it, then becomes Registered, Waitlisted, or Declined. After the meet it moves to Completed, so over time My Meets becomes a record of where you have competed.

My Meets
5
Watch live

The scoreboard page updates as judges enter scores. If you are at the venue you can also enter the join code on Join a Meet and see the Next Up list, including the weights and heights for each athlete, without being able to change anything.

Join a Meet
MEET-DAY CREW
Volunteers & Judges

You do not need an account. The promoter gives you a six-character code, you pick what you are doing that day, and the app opens already set up for your job.

1
Enter the join code

Open Join a Meet and type the code. The meet name comes back so you can check it is the right one.

Join a Meet
2
Pick your role

Athlete or Spectator shows the standings and who is up next, with nothing to tap by accident. Volunteer is for pit crew and shows the plate loading calculator. Judge and Promoter need the admin PIN from the promoter; you type it once and the phone remembers which role you chose.

3
Judges: score from the pad

Pick the event and the athletes come up in the right order. Enter reps, time, distance, the bar height reached or stone splits, depending on the event. Scores go to the scoreboard the moment the phone has signal.

4
Pit crew: load from Next Up

Next Up shows who is lifting, the weight they need, the plates to put on each side and any rack or pin height, so nobody is doing plate maths at the bar. The promoter decides whether you can change the bar weight or enter a custom load.

5
Lose signal? Keep going

The app keeps working with no signal. Anything you enter is held on the phone and sent as soon as it reconnects, so a dead spot in the gym does not cost you any scores.

COMMON QUESTIONS
FAQ
EVERYONE
Does it cost anything?
No. Finding shows, registering, running a meet, the live scoreboard and the gym directory are all free right now. If that changes for any part of it, the price will be on the page before you use it, and what is already free for athletes stays free.
Does it work without Wi-Fi?
Yes. Scoring happens on the phone and is held there until it can be sent. A judge can score a whole event with no signal, and the public scoreboard catches up when the phone reconnects.
Do I need to install an app?
No. Everything runs in the browser on any phone, tablet or laptop. Promoters and judges can add the scorer to the home screen so it opens like an app, but nothing is downloaded from a store. Open the scorer
I forgot my password.
On the sign-in form, enter your email and tap Forgot password. The email you get has a link that brings you back to the Account page to choose a new one. If you are already signed in, use Change password on the same page. Account
What happens to my data?
What you enter when you register goes to the promoter of that meet, and ZeroTacky keeps what it needs to run the service. Your email is never shown publicly. The Privacy Policy lists what is kept and for how long. Privacy Policy
ATHLETES AND SPECTATORS
Do I need an account to register for a show?
Yes, a free one, and you can create it right on the registration form without leaving the page. The entry is tied to your account: it shows on My Meets so you can see when the promoter accepts it, and after the meet it stays there as part of your record. You need to be 12 or older on the day of the meet; under 18, a parent or guardian creates the account, registers you and completes their part of the waiver. Find a Show
How do I watch a show live?
Open the show page and tap the live scoreboard link. It shows standings, each event and who is up next, and updates as judges score. No account, no code. If you are at the venue, the promoter can also give you the join code, which adds the Next Up list with each athlete's weights.
What shows up publicly about me?
Once the promoter accepts you, your name and division appear on the meet roster and the live scoreboard, the same as a printed start list. Your email, date of birth and emergency contact go to the promoter only. Nothing else is public unless you turn on your own athlete page.
How do I get my own athlete page?
On your Account page, pick a username and turn on Show my profile publicly. Your name, photo, roles, location, home gym, favorite lift, PRs and the social handles you added show at zerotacky.com/athletes/yourname and in the Athletes list. Turn it off any time and the page is gone. Athletes
PROMOTERS
What do I need to run a show on ZeroTacky?
An account with Promoter ticked, your phone or a laptop to set the meet up, and one phone per judge on the day. Nothing is installed and the gym does not need Wi-Fi. The first-show guide walks through the whole thing with pictures. Set up your first show
Join code or admin PIN: who gets which?
Two codes, two jobs. The six-character join code gets a phone into your meet; give it to everyone helping, and to athletes or spectators who want the Next Up list. The admin PIN lets a joined phone score and change the setup; give it to judges and your co-promoters only. The join code is on the Meet Day tab; the PIN is set on the Meet tab.
Can other people help me run it?
Yes. Anyone with the join code and the admin PIN can judge or edit from their phone; several phones can score different stations at the same time and everything merges. The meet itself belongs to your account, so only you can list, unlist or delete it.
How do athletes get on the roster?
Two ways, and you can mix them. Open registration on the Listing tab and athletes register from the show page; each entry appears on your Registrations tab and you accept or decline it (Waitlist Only on the Listing tab holds new entries instead). Or type athletes straight into the roster in Meet Setup, which is what most people do for a small show or for day-of entries.
Can I unlist or delete a meet?
Unlist any time from the Listing tab; the meet stays yours, it just leaves Find a Show. Delete from the Meet Day tab as long as the meet is not running or finished; if it already has athletes or results you type its name to confirm. Finished meets are kept so results stay available. My Meets
GYM OWNERS
My gym is in the directory. How do I claim it?
Open the gym's page and tap Claim this gym, then give your name, email and role at the gym. Sign in first and the approved listing attaches to your account straight away; otherwise we confirm by email. We check each claim against the gym's own site or contact address. Once approved, the listing is yours to edit from My Gym: equipment, day passes, drop-in hours, website and contact. Gym Directory
My gym is not listed. How do I add it?
Sign in, tick Gym owner on your Account page, and use Add my gym. It goes into a short review queue so the directory stays real gyms with real equipment, then appears under your account. Add my gym
NOT HERE YET
What's coming

Everything above is live today and free. These are the next pieces, in roughly the order we plan to build them.

Paid show registration

Promoters set an entry fee and athletes pay when they register, instead of settling up separately.

Day passes from the gym directory

Buy a drop-in pass for a listed gym from its page, so travelling athletes can train on the way to a show.

Trainer directory

Coaches who train in person or online get their own searchable list, built from the trainer flag on athlete profiles.

Show history on athlete pages

Meets you competed in, with placings, listed on your public page once the promoter marks the show complete.

Gyms and shows linked both ways

A show page points at its host gym, and a gym page lists the shows it has hosted.

TACKY

ZEROTACKY

TACKY
HOME
HOW IT WORKS
FIND A SHOW
GYM DIRECTORY
ATHLETES
ACCOUNT
JOIN A MEET
How It Works
 PROMOTER GUIDE
Set up your first show

This walks one made-up meet, the Iron Harbor Classic, from a blank screen to meet day. Every screen below is the real one you will use, and each step says what it changes for athletes and spectators. Budget about half an hour the first time.

WHAT YOU NEED
A ZeroTacky account with Promoter ticked on the Account page. The meet belongs to that account, so it follows you from laptop to phone and only you can change it.
A laptop for the setup. The phone scorer can build the meet itself under Meet Setup (divisions, stations, events, athletes), but Listing and Registrations live on My Meets only, and the tabs are easier to read on a bigger screen.
On the day: one phone per judge and one for the pit crew. Volunteers do not need accounts; they join with a code you hand out in step 9.

1
MY MEETS, NEW MEET
Create the meet

Open My Meets and tap New Meet. It asks for the name, the competition date and an optional web address. The address (the slug) becomes zerotacky.com/shows/your-slug; leave it blank and one is made from the name.

Create & Open Meet saves the meet to your account and opens it as eight numbered tabs. The order of the tabs is the order you fill them in.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Nothing yet. A new meet starts unlisted, so it is not in Find a Show and has no show page until you tick Listed in step 6. Its registration page and live scoreboard do open by direct link, which is handy for checking your work before anyone else sees it.

My Meets
2
TAB 1, MEET
Meet details and rules

The admin PIN is four to six digits. Judges and anyone who needs to change the setup on meet day type it once on their phone, after the join code from step 9. Collar weight is per pair and is added to every bar load the pit crew calculator shows.

Athlete run order decides who lifts when. Reverse Overall Points is the usual choice: the leader goes last so the podium race builds. Reverse Previous Event looks only at the last event. Roster Order never reshuffles. The screen explains each one under the buttons.

The tiebreaker only matters when two athletes finish on the same points. Available Gym Plates tells the pit crew calculator what it is allowed to use; turn off anything the gym does not own.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

The run order drives the Next Up queue on volunteer phones; the public scoreboard only shows who is Up Now on each station. Plates and collars drive the loads the pit crew sees. None of this is shown to athletes directly.

3
TAB 2, DIVISIONS
Divisions

Add one division per weight class or experience group, named the way athletes expect to read them. Type a name and press Add; the arrows reorder them.

The order here is the order they appear everywhere else: the registration dropdown, the scoreboard and the show card. Edits sit in working memory until you press Save Changes in the banner at the bottom.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Division names show as chips on the show card in Find a Show, as the choices on the registration form and as the sections of the live scoreboard.

4
TAB 3, STATIONS
Stations and floor plan

A station is one set of implements running its own order. Divisions on the same station run back to back; two stations run at the same time in different parts of the gym.

A small meet is fine on one station. Most promoters decide this after sign-ups close, when they know how many athletes each division has. Rename the stations if the gym calls them something else. If one station runs the events in a different order from the rest, the arrows on its card set that order.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Each station gets an Up Now strip at the top of the scoreboard, so spectators can see who is lifting where. Next Up on the volunteer phones is per station.

5
TAB 4, EVENTS
Events

Add Event opens the form. Pick how it is scored (reps, max weight, time or distance, time or implements), set the time cap and lanes, then tell the loader how the implement works: load points is how many places plates go on, tare is what the empty implement weighs. Those two numbers are what make the pit crew plate maths right.

Under per-division weights, enter the target weight for each division. Add a callout title if the pit crew should see a note, for example the keg or the pin height. Save Event, then Save Changes.

Events run in the order listed. Use the arrows on the cards if the running order changes.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Implement names show as chips on the show card. The registration page lists every division with its target weight for each event, so athletes know what they are signing up to lift. In the TV layout the scoreboard gets one column per event.

6
TAB 5, ATHLETES
Athletes

There are two ways onto the roster. Athletes who register online land here when you accept them in step 8. Paper sign-ups and walk-ins you add yourself: Bulk Add takes one name per line into a division, Single Add takes one at a time.

Each athlete gets a lot number inside their division. That is the order for the first event, and the fallback order whenever two athletes are level. The one exception is Reverse Previous Event, which breaks a tie on the last event by overall points first and lot number second.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

Roster names appear on the live scoreboard as soon as the meet is listed, with a dash in every event column until scores come in. Add only athletes you expect to show up.

7
TAB 6, LISTING
List it and open entries

Tick Listed to put the meet in Find a Show. The three status dropdowns are the badges the public sees: competition status (upcoming, live, completed), registration status (open, waitlist, closed, day-of only) and results status.

Fill in the venue, the federation or format, the entry fee as you want it displayed, the deadline, an athlete cap and a contact. No money moves through the site; the fee line tells athletes how you want to be paid. Save Listing Settings writes it straight to the server.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

This tab is the public face of the show. The card in Find a Show, the show page and the top of the registration page are all built from it, and the capacity line counts every athlete on the roster against your cap, including the ones you added by hand.

Find a Show
The card athletes see in Find a Show.
The show page at zerotacky.com/shows/your-slug.
8
TAB 7, REGISTRATIONS
Approve registrations

An athlete signs in or creates a free account on the form, picks a division, gives a name, email, emergency contact and date of birth, signs the waiver and submits. The entry is tied to their account, which is how it shows on their My Meets page. Under-18s are entered by a parent or guardian from the guardian's account.

Each entry shows up here as Pending with the division and the signed waiver. Accept adds the athlete to that division roster with the next lot number; Decline removes them. Emergency contacts and dates of birth are visible to you only.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

The athlete sees Pending, then Registered or Declined, on their My Meets page. An entry only takes a spot on the capacity line once you accept it and it joins the roster; pending entries do not count.

What the athlete sees first: the account step.
Then the entry form, with name and email filled from the account.
What you see.
9
TAB 8, MEET DAY
Meet day codes and screens

The six-character join code is how volunteer phones attach to your meet. Print Both gives you two QR codes for the gym wall: one for judges and pit crew, one for the live scoreboard. Rotate the code if it gets out to people who should not have it; phones signed in to your account are unaffected.

Volunteers open Join a Meet, enter the code and pick a role. Athlete and Spectator are read-only. Pit crew get the loading calculator. Judge and Promoter also type the admin PIN from step 2.

Your own phone joins the same way: open the join link, pick Promoter and enter the admin PIN. Opening the scorer on its own shows whatever meet that phone had last, so always come in through the join link. The TV link is a full-width standings table for a laptop plugged into the gym TV.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

The scoreboard link is public and needs no sign-in. Share it with spectators and put the TV layout on a screen in the gym.

Join a Meet
What a volunteer sees after scanning the join QR.
10
ZEROTACKY.COM/M/YOUR-SLUG
The live scoreboard

As judges score, the board updates on every phone and TV that has it open. On a phone each division shows standing cards plus the current event. The TV layout, from the Phone/TV button in the header or the TV link on Meet Day, gives each division its own table with one column per event and the total on the right. In both, the strips at the top show who is up on each station and the chips filter to one division.

When the last event is in, go back to the Listing tab and set competition status to Completed and results to Final. The show moves to Completed on every athlete's My Meets page and the standings stay up as the record of the day.

ON THE PUBLIC SIDE

This is the page spectators share. It works on any phone with no app and no account, and it keeps the final standings after the show.

See a demo board
The TV layout. On a phone the same board shows standing cards.
After the show

Set the statuses to Completed and Final on the Listing tab and the show becomes a record: the public page and scoreboard stay up, and it moves to Completed on every athlete's My Meets. A video walkthrough of this guide is coming after our first full show.

ZeroTacky Terms of Use
DRAFT FOR LEGAL REVIEW. Working draft for ZeroTacky; a qualified attorney should review it before it is relied on.

Effective date: October 2026
Operator: ZeroTacky, operated from the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, United States ("ZeroTacky", "we")

1. Agreement

By creating an account, registering for a competition, publishing or scoring a meet, or otherwise using zerotacky.com and the ZeroTacky meet-day scoring app (together, the "Service"), you agree to these Terms and to our Privacy Policy. If you do not agree, do not use the Service.

2. What ZeroTacky is, and is not

ZeroTacky is software: a directory of strongman competitions, an athlete registration tool, and a scoring app that promoters and their volunteers run on their own phones on meet day.

ZeroTacky is not the organizer of any competition. Unless a competition page says otherwise, we do not organize, sanction, insure, supervise or officiate the competitions listed on the Service. The promoter does.
No safety or medical advice. Plate-loading math, implement weights and rack-height callouts in the Service are conveniences. Promoters, judges, loaders and athletes are responsible for checking bar weights, collars, pins and the course before every attempt.
Results are the promoter's. Scores and standings shown by the Service are entered by the promoter's judges. The promoter decides the official results and may correct them.
3. Accounts and age
You must be at least 13 years old to create an account. If you are under 18, a parent or legal guardian must agree to these Terms for you, and must complete any competition registration on your behalf (see section 4).
You are responsible for your login, and for any publish key, join code or admin PIN a promoter gives you. Do not share them beyond the people running the meet.
One person, one account. Keep your email address current; we use it for sign-in and for messages about your registrations.
You may close your account at any time from the account page or by emailing us (section 10). Competition records you appear in may remain in the promoter's results (section 7).
4. Registering for a competition
Registering on ZeroTacky sends a request to the promoter. The promoter accepts, declines or waitlists it. A request is not a confirmed entry until the promoter accepts it.
You must accept the competition waiver to register. The waiver is between you, the promoter, the venue and ZeroTacky, and is shown in full before you submit.
Athletes under 18 may not register themselves. A parent or legal guardian must complete the registration, accept the waiver on the athlete's behalf, and may be required by the promoter to attend check-in and sign on paper. Promoters set the minimum age for their competitions.
Entry fees, refunds, weigh-ins, membership cards and disputes are between you and the promoter. ZeroTacky does not currently collect payments.
Give accurate information. Promoters rely on your emergency contact on meet day.
5. Promoters

If you publish or score a meet on ZeroTacky you confirm that:

you are responsible for the safety, insurance, venue permission, rules, officiating, medical coverage and results of your event, and for deciding whether your event needs a waiver beyond the one shown by the Service;
you will use athlete registration data (names, emails, emergency contacts, bodyweights) only to run the competition the athlete registered for, and will delete or stop using it when it is no longer needed for that purpose;
you have the right to publish the event details, division names and results you upload;
you will keep your publish key, join codes and admin PIN to the people running your meet, and tell us if one leaks;
you will keep your own backup of your meet (the Service offers a JSON backup and CSV export) and will not rely on the Service as your only record.
6. Acceptable use

Do not: submit false or impersonated registrations; guess or brute-force another meet's codes, keys or PINs; interfere with live scoring; scrape athlete contact details; upload content you do not have the right to publish; or use the Service for anything unlawful. We may suspend or close accounts and remove meets that break these Terms or disrupt a live competition.

7. Public results and your name

Promoters may publicly list their meets. For a listed or published meet, division rosters, athlete names, bodyweight classes, scores and placings are public on the Service and may stay in the competition archive. Email addresses and emergency contacts are never public. If you want your name removed from a past result, contact the promoter first; if that fails, contact us (section 10) and we will work it out with the promoter.

8. Free of charge, "as is"

The Service is currently free. THE SERVICE IS PROVIDED "AS IS" AND "AS AVAILABLE", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NON-INFRINGEMENT. WE DO NOT PROMISE THAT THE SERVICE WILL BE UNINTERRUPTED, ERROR-FREE OR FREE OF DATA LOSS. Scores entered on a phone that is offline are queued on that phone and may be lost if the phone is lost, reset or offline for a long time.

9. Limitation of liability

TO THE FULLEST EXTENT THE LAW ALLOWS, ZEROTACKY AND ITS OPERATOR ARE NOT LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, OR FOR LOST PROFITS, DATA OR GOODWILL, OR FOR PERSONAL INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE, ARISING FROM (1) YOUR PARTICIPATION IN ANY COMPETITION OR TRAINING, (2) ANY SCORING ERROR, LOADING CALCULATION, RACK-HEIGHT CALLOUT OR SYNC DELAY, OR (3) YOUR USE OF OR INABILITY TO USE THE SERVICE. OUR TOTAL LIABILITY FOR ALL CLAIMS IS LIMITED TO THE GREATER OF ONE HUNDRED U.S. DOLLARS ($100) OR THE AMOUNT YOU PAID ZEROTACKY IN THE TWELVE MONTHS BEFORE THE CLAIM. Some states do not allow some of these limits; in those states they apply as far as the law allows.

10. Contact and changes

Questions, deletion requests and complaints: privacy@zerotacky.com. If we change these Terms in a way that matters, we will update the effective date and tell account holders by email before the change takes effect. Continuing to use the Service after that is acceptance of the new Terms.

11. Governing law and venue

These Terms are governed by the law of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, without regard to conflict-of-laws rules. Disputes about these Terms or the Service go to the state or federal courts in or serving York County, Pennsylvania, and you consent to their jurisdiction. Nothing in this section changes the governing law stated in a competition waiver.

ZeroTacky Privacy Policy
DRAFT FOR LEGAL REVIEW. Working draft for ZeroTacky; a qualified attorney should review it before it is relied on.

Effective date: October 2026
Operator: ZeroTacky, operated from the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, United States
Contact: privacy@zerotacky.com

1. What ZeroTacky is

ZeroTacky is a public directory of strongman competitions, an athlete registration tool, and an offline-first scoring app that promoters run on their own phones on meet day. This policy covers all of it.

2. What we collect and why
WHO	WHAT	WHY	WHERE IT COMES FROM
Anyone with an account (athletes, promoters)	Email address, display name, password (stored hashed by our authentication provider), sign-in timestamps	To sign you in, let promoters manage their meets, and send you messages about your registrations	You
Athletes who register for a competition	Name, email, emergency contact (name and phone), the division you chose, optional bodyweight, your date of birth, the date and time you accepted the waiver and an identifier of the exact waiver text you accepted; for an athlete under 18 on competition day, the parent or guardian's name and contact	To send your entry to the promoter, put you on the roster when accepted, and give the promoter your emergency contact on meet day	You, or your parent or guardian
Athletes on a meet roster (added by a promoter, with or without an account)	Name, division, lot number, optional bodyweight and rack heights, scores and placings	To run and score the meet and show standings	The promoter and their judges
Everyone who visits	Standard server logs (IP address, browser type, pages requested, timestamps) kept by our hosting provider; the IP address of a device that submits a registration or tries a PIN, kept for about a day to stop abuse	To keep the site running and stop brute-force and spam	Your browser

We do not run advertising trackers or sell data. We do not collect payment details; entry fees are between you and the promoter.

3. Cookies and storage on your device
Sign-in: a session token from our authentication provider (Supabase Auth) keeps you signed in.
Local storage: your theme and layout choice, and, if you use the scoring app (/scorer, /join), the meet you are working on, recovery snapshots and a queue of scores waiting to sync. Scores entered while the gym Wi-Fi is down stay on the phone and are sent when it reconnects. Clearing your browser data removes them.
No third-party advertising or cross-site tracking cookies.
4. Who sees your data
Promoters. When you register for a competition, the promoter of that competition gets your registration (name, email, emergency contact, date of birth, division, bodyweight if given, waiver acceptance, and guardian details for an athlete under 18). Promoters agree to use it only to run that competition.
The public. For a meet the promoter has listed or published, rosters, athlete names, divisions, scores and placings are public on /shows/<meet> and the live scoreboard /m/<meet>. Emails, emergency contacts and guardian details are never public.
Our providers. Vercel (hosting, United States), Supabase (database and authentication, United States) and Resend (transactional email, United States) process data for us under their own terms. We do not share data with anyone else except as the law requires.
5. How long we keep it
Account data: while your account exists. Close your account and we delete the profile within 30 days; your name may remain in competition results you took part in (below).
Registrations: until the promoter deletes the meet, or until you ask us to remove yours.
Results: published competition results are part of the sport's record and stay up unless the promoter removes the meet or you ask for your name to be removed from a past result.
Abuse-prevention IP records: about a day. Server logs: per our hosting provider's retention.
6. Your choices

Email privacy@zerotacky.com to see what we hold about you, correct it, delete your account or registrations, or have your name removed from a past result. We answer within 30 days. We may need to confirm you are the account holder first. Residents of states with privacy laws that give extra rights (for example California) can exercise them the same way.

7. Children

Nobody under 13 may create an account, and we do not knowingly collect information about anyone under 13. Athletes under 18 are registered for competitions by a parent or legal guardian, who provides the information in section 2. If you believe a child has given us information without a guardian's involvement, email us and we will delete it.

8. Security

Data is encrypted in transit; passwords are hashed by Supabase Auth; database access is restricted by row-level rules so promoters see only their own meets and athlete contact details are never readable by the public. No system is perfectly secure; if we learn of a breach affecting you we will tell you as the law requires.

9. Changes

If we change this policy in a way that matters (for example, when we add payments), we will update the effective date and email account holders before the change takes effect.

Strongman Competition Assumption of Risk, Release of Liability, Waiver and Indemnity Agreement
DRAFT FOR LEGAL REVIEW. This is the waiver shown during athlete registration on ZeroTacky. Promoters and the operator should have a qualified attorney review it for the venue, insurance policy and state law that apply to each competition before relying on it.

Competition: {{EVENT_NAME}}
Competition date: {{EVENT_DATE}}
Promoter / organizer: {{PROMOTER_NAME}}
Venue: {{VENUE_NAME_AND_ADDRESS}}

In this agreement, "I" and "me" mean the athlete, or, if the athlete is under 18, the athlete's parent or legal guardian signing on the athlete's behalf (see section 7). "Released Parties" means everyone listed in section 4.

1. The risks of strongman competition

I understand that competing in and warming up for strongman events, including overhead pressing (logs, axles, circus dumbbells, kegs), deadlifts, moving events (yokes, farmer's walks, Husafell stones, sandbags, vehicle and harness pulls) and loading events (Atlas stones, kegs, natural stones), involves heavy, awkward and moving implements and maximal physical effort.

I understand that these risks cannot be removed no matter how careful the Promoter, the Venue, the judges or the loaders are. They include, without limitation:

muscle tears, tendon and ligament ruptures (biceps, patellar, Achilles, rotator cuff), spinal injuries, hernias, fractures, concussions and crush injuries from dropped or shifting implements;
cardiovascular events, heat illness, blacking out under load, cuts and skin tears;
equipment failure, rack or yoke pins set at the wrong height, plates or collars slipping, uneven or wet floors and parking surfaces, and mistakes by volunteer loaders, spotters or judges;
permanent disability and death.
2. My fitness and my duty to inspect

I state that I am in good health, have trained for the weights and events of this competition, and have no medical condition that makes my participation unsafe. I am responsible for inspecting the course, the rack and yoke heights and the implements before each attempt, and for telling a judge or the Promoter at once if I believe anything is unsafe. I will follow the rules of the competition and the instructions of the judges and staff.

3. Medical treatment

If I am injured or have a medical emergency at the competition, I authorize the Promoter, Venue staff and medical personnel to give first aid and to arrange emergency transport and treatment. I am responsible for all medical, ambulance and hospital costs incurred for me.

4. Assumption of risk and release

In exchange for being allowed to register for and compete in {{EVENT_NAME}}, I voluntarily accept all risks of participating, known and unknown. On behalf of myself, my heirs, assigns and personal representatives, I release, waive, discharge and agree not to sue:

{{PROMOTER_NAME}} and its owners, officers, event staff, judges, loaders, spotters and volunteers;
the owner and operator of {{VENUE_NAME_AND_ADDRESS}} and their staff; and
ZeroTacky, the registration and scoring software provider, and its owner, operator and contributors,

from all liability, claims, demands and causes of action for any loss, damage, injury or death I suffer while participating in, warming up for, traveling to or from, or attending the competition, including loss caused by the ordinary negligence of any Released Party, to the fullest extent the law allows.

5. Indemnity

I agree to indemnify and hold harmless the Released Parties from any claim, loss, cost or expense (including reasonable attorney's fees) brought by me or on my behalf, or by any third party, arising from my participation in the competition or from my breach of this agreement, to the fullest extent the law allows.

6. Results, name and image

I agree that the Promoter and ZeroTacky may record and publish my name, division, bodyweight class, scores and placings, and photographs and video of me at the competition, on live scoreboards, in competition archives and in promotion of the competition and of ZeroTacky, without payment to me.

7. Athletes under 18

An athlete under 18 may not register on their own. If the athlete is under 18, I confirm that I am the athlete's parent or court-appointed legal guardian, that I am completing this registration for the athlete, that I have read this agreement, and that I agree to it both on the athlete's behalf and on my own behalf, including the release in section 4 and the indemnity in section 5 for any claim the athlete may later bring. I understand the Promoter may require my presence and a paper signature at check-in before the athlete competes, and that the Promoter sets the minimum age for this competition. I will give the Promoter my name and a way to reach me.

8. Scoring software

I understand that ZeroTacky is software run by the Promoter and its volunteers. Scores, standings, plate-loading calculations and rack-height callouts shown by the software are tools for the Promoter; the Promoter and the judges decide results and are responsible for checking weights and equipment. Scores may be delayed, corrected or lost if a device is offline. I release ZeroTacky from any claim about scoring errors, lost data or placings.

9. Electronic acceptance, copies and general terms

By checking the acceptance box and submitting my registration I sign this agreement electronically, and I agree that this has the same effect as a handwritten signature. ZeroTacky records the date and time of my acceptance and an identifier of the exact text I accepted. The current text is available at any time at zerotacky.com/legal/waiver; I can print or save it from that page or ask the Promoter for a copy.

I have read this agreement, I understand that I am giving up substantial legal rights by signing it, and I sign it freely. If any part of it is held invalid, the rest stays in force. This agreement is governed by the law of the state where the competition is held, unless the Promoter's own registration terms say otherwise.

This is the template. The copy you accept when registering has the competition, date, promoter and venue filled in, and its version id is stored with your registration.
